note: Maintained daily. Every item links to the page that confirms it.

happened.title: Fox News: Collins and Jackson tied 49-49 in Maine; Saint Anselm has Pappas up 7
happened.what: A Fox News poll of 1,514 Maine likely voters taken Oct. 16-20 finds Troy Jackson and Sen. Susan Collins tied 49-49 (Jackson 50-48 among registered voters) and Hannah Pingree leading the governor race 49-39 with independent Rick Bennett at 9; the same week's Fox polls had Paxton and Talarico tied 49-49 in Texas and Brown ahead 52-47 in Ohio. Saint Anselm's Oct. 19-20 survey of 1,672 New Hampshire likely voters has Chris Pappas over John E. Sununu 50-43 and Kelly Ayotte over Cinde Warmington 50-42.
happened.why: Maine is one of Cook's seven Senate Toss Ups; a tie with Collins at 49 keeps a Democratic pickup there in doubt while New Hampshire, a Democratic-held seat, looks safer for them.
happened.src: Fox News (Beacon Research/Shaw & Co.), Oct 22; Saint Anselm College Survey Center, Oct 22

happened.title: Judge curbs DHS noncitizen-voting probes in nine states
happened.what: Federal Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín ruled late Oct. 21 that the Department of Homeland Security's 'Unlawful Voter Initiative' may not conduct field operations or interviews likely to involve U.S. citizens in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin, citing 'substantial evidence' of 'intimidating conduct' and a 'high likelihood of error' because no federal database holds citizenship status; DHS said it has 'no plans to question or investigate people we believe to be U.S. citizens.' The suit was brought by nonprofits and local governments, separate from the Democratic leaders' Oct. 21 case over federal 'noncitizen' voter lists.
happened.why: The order limits door-to-door federal activity during early voting in five states with competitive Senate or governor races and most of the House battleground.

happened.title: Senate Leadership Fund buys its first Mississippi ads
happened.what: CNN reports Senate Leadership Fund placed an initial reservation of about $160,000 in Mississippi for Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith against Democrat Scott Colom, with more expected; Senate Democrats announced about $1 million in ads after Senate Majority PAC's $1.2 million reservation, American Bridge plans $2.1 million, and AdImpact expects about $8 million of spending from October through Election Day, Democrats ahead roughly $5 million to $2.7 million.
happened.why: The main Senate Republican super PAC is now spending in a seat no rater had in play a month ago, a further sign that the party is defending rather than expanding the map.
happened.src: CNN (Sarah Ferris, Manu Raju and David Wright) via KESQ, Oct 22

happened.title: Crystal Ball moves Ohio governor to Leans Democratic, Michigan to Likely Democratic
happened.what: Sabato's Crystal Ball shifted Ohio's governor race from Toss-up to Leans Democratic, citing Amy Acton's public polling lead and the backlash to Vivek Ramaswamy's ad about her estranged mother, moved Michigan from Leans to Likely Democratic after allies of John James cut their spending, and moved Alabama and Oklahoma from Safe to Likely Republican; its tally is 26 governorships at least leaning Democratic, 22 at least leaning Republican and two Toss-ups, Nevada and Georgia.
happened.why: The rater says Democrats 'appear to be on the cusp of claiming a majority of the nation's governorships,' and Ohio is the first Toss-up governor race to move off the fence this month.
happened.src: Sabato's Crystal Ball (Kyle Kondik and J. Miles Coleman), Oct 22

happened.title: MAGA Inc. network commits $277 million to the final weeks
happened.what: Reuters reports Trump-aligned super PACs have committed more than $277 million to television and mail over the campaign's final six weeks, with MAGA Inc. routing $225 million through two affiliated groups, including more than $36 million in Texas for Ken Paxton, $30.1 million in Michigan for Mike Rogers and more than $28 million in Ohio for Jon Husted; MAGA Inc. reported $164 million in cash.
happened.why: The Trump network is now the largest outside spender in three Toss Up Senate races, outside the FEC totals the app shows for party committees.
happened.src: Reuters (Virginia Furness) via Hawaii Tribune-Herald, Oct 22

happened.title: Vance defends Ramaswamy's ad about Acton's mother as Republicans split
happened.what: Vice President Vance told Axios he was 'a little bit disgusted' by Republicans criticizing Vivek Ramaswamy's television ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother and told them to stop whining; Jon Husted said 'I would not have run that ad,' Nikki Haley called Ramaswamy 'a bad guy,' and Acton's campaign says the ad cost $4 million.
happened.why: The intraparty fight over the ad coincides with Crystal Ball moving the Ohio governor race to Leans Democratic and gives Democrats a closing argument in a state with a Toss Up Senate race on the same ballot.

happened.title: Cook battleground polls: Democrats lead the Iowa, Ohio and Texas Senate races
happened.what: Surveys by New River Strategies (D) and GS Strategy Group (R) for the Cook Political Report, taken Oct. 9-13 among likely voters, found Josh Turek 46-44 over Ashley Hinson in Iowa (Libertarian Thomas Laehn 8; n=602), Sherrod Brown 49-43 over Jon Husted in Ohio (n=959) and James Talarico 49-44 over Ken Paxton in Texas (n=934), with Rob Sand 54-43, Amy Acton 49-44 and Greg Abbott 48-46 in the governor races.
happened.why: Bipartisan polling for the rater that lists all three as Toss Ups has Democrats ahead in every Republican-held seat they need for the majority.

happened.title: Senate Republicans eye Mississippi rescue as SLF's Ohio reservation grows to $93 million
happened.what: Axios reports Senate Republicans weighing a cash infusion for Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi plus more for South Carolina and Kansas; AdImpact figures show Senate Leadership Fund's South Carolina buy grew from $5 million to $8.5 million, its Ohio reservations from $28 million to $93 million and Iowa from $11 million to $53 million, with $14 million earmarked for Kansas, while the NRSC took a $20 million loan after raising $31.4 million in September and Trump pledged another $100 million to his super PACs.
happened.why: Republican money is being pulled into seats no rater had in play a month ago, a sign the party is defending rather than expanding the Senate map.
happened.src: Axios (Hans Nichols, Marc Caputo and Stef Kight), Oct 21

happened.title: NYT/Siena: Democrats lead the House ballot 52-41 among likely voters
happened.what: The New York Times/Siena national poll of more than 3,000 voters, released Oct. 21, finds Democrats ahead of Republicans by 10 points on the congressional ballot when every candidate's name is offered (52-41 in the Times' topline, per Fox News and the RealClearPolling table), leading by 5 in the 35 states with Senate races, with Trump's job approval at 36-59.
happened.why: The highest-rated national poll of the cycle lands two points above the polling average, and its Senate-state figure suggests the map's tilt toward Republicans is being overcome.
happened.src: Siena College Research Institute, Oct 21; Fox News live blog, Oct 21

happened.title: Inside Elections shifts 30 races toward Democrats, Texas Senate to Toss-up
happened.what: Inside Elections moved five Senate races (Texas Tilt R to Toss-up, New Hampshire Toss-up to Tilt D, Kansas Likely to Tilt R, South Carolina Likely to Lean R, Florida Solid to Likely R), 22 House races (NC-01, NC-11, OH-09, IA-02 and TX-15 to Toss-up; AZ-01, PA-07 and PA-08 to Tilt D) and three governor races (Texas Likely to Lean R, Nebraska and Vermont Solid to Likely R), projecting a Democratic Senate gain of three to five seats and a House gain of 10 to 20.
happened.why: The rater that had been most favorable to Republicans now puts the four-seat Senate gain Democrats need inside its range and says Democrats have no defensive Senate seat rated Toss-up or worse.

happened.title: Crystal Ball: 223 House seats now at least lean Democratic after 28 changes
happened.what: Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 28 House ratings, pushing seats at least leaning Democratic to 223 against 200 at least leaning Republican and 12 Toss-ups: IA-03, IA-02, WI-03, PA-10, AZ-06, CO-08, AZ-01, NC-01 and NC-11 went from Toss-up to Leans Democratic, TX-35 to Toss-up, and TX-23, NV-02, SC-01 and MN-01 to Leans Republican.
happened.why: For the first time this cycle a major rater has more than 218 seats leaning to Democrats, so Republicans would need to win seats currently rated against them to keep the House.

happened.title: Cook moves South Carolina and Mississippi toward Democrats, Minnesota toward Republicans
happened.what: The Cook Political Report shifted South Carolina from Likely to Lean Republican, Mississippi from Solid to Likely Republican and Minnesota from Likely to Lean Democratic, writing that recent polling shows Peggy Flanagan 'slightly underperforming where she should be given the national environment'; its Senate page now lists seven Toss Ups (Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas), six of them Republican-held.
happened.why: Cook says the moves do not change its overall Senate outlook, but Minnesota becomes the one Democratic-held seat where the rater sees the candidate lagging the environment.

upcoming.title: Arizona mail-ballot request deadline
upcoming.what: Oct. 23 is the last day to request a mail ballot in Arizona; Oct. 27 is the last recommended day to mail it back, and in-person early voting ends Oct. 30.
upcoming.why: Arizona's governor race, rated Lean Democrat by Cook, and the AZ-01 and AZ-06 House seats are on the competitive list.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan final October consumer sentiment
upcoming.what: The University of Michigan releases its final October consumer-sentiment reading; the preliminary figure was 46.3, near the survey's record low.
upcoming.why: It is the last sentiment reading before Election Day in a campaign dominated by prices, with gasoline above $4.

upcoming.title: Michigan statewide early voting begins
upcoming.what: Early in-person voting sites open statewide in Michigan, open at least eight hours a day through Nov. 1, with some communities offering extra days.
upcoming.why: Early votes start in the open Senate and governor races and in House battlegrounds such as MI-04 and MI-07.

upcoming.title: Florida mandatory early voting begins
upcoming.what: Florida's mandatory early voting period runs Oct. 24 through Oct. 31, and counties may offer additional days or hours.
upcoming.why: Early votes begin in the Senate race, a governor race Cook moved to Lean Republican, and House seats such as FL-13 and FL-27.

upcoming.title: Obama rallies in Cleveland and Detroit
upcoming.what: Former President Barack Obama is to campaign in Cleveland with Sherrod Brown and Amy Acton and in Detroit with Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson on Oct. 24, the first Saturday of Michigan's statewide early voting; venues and times are to be announced.
upcoming.why: Ohio's Senate and governor races and Michigan's Senate race are Cook Toss Ups, and Trump and Vance have each campaigned in both states in October.

upcoming.title: New York and New Jersey early voting begins
upcoming.what: Early in-person voting runs Oct. 24 through Nov. 1 in both states; Oct. 24 is also New York's deadline for registration and for mailed or online early mail-ballot applications.
upcoming.why: Early votes begin in House battlegrounds including NY-17, a Cook Toss Up, and NJ-07, where the main House GOP super PAC cut its ads.
upcoming.src: New Jersey Division of Elections, accessed Oct 19; Stony Brook University, accessed Oct 19

upcoming.title: Harris campaigns in New Hampshire for Pappas
upcoming.what: Former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigns in New Hampshire for Senate nominee Chris Pappas on Oct. 24, part of a five-state swing that also takes her to Wisconsin for David Crowley on Oct. 26 and to Georgia for three days from Oct. 28 for Sen. Jon Ossoff.
upcoming.why: New Hampshire is one of the two Democratic-held Senate seats rated Lean Democratic, and the swing puts a 2024 nominee into the final-week closing argument in three battlegrounds.

upcoming.title: Pennsylvania mail ballot application deadline
upcoming.what: Oct. 27 is the deadline to apply for a mail-in or absentee ballot in Pennsylvania, and completed ballots must reach county election offices by 8 p.m. on Nov. 3.
upcoming.why: Pennsylvania's House battlegrounds, including PA-01, PA-07 and PA-08, could help decide House control.
upcoming.src: Pennsylvania Department of State, accessed Oct 13

upcoming.title: Ohio absentee application deadline
upcoming.what: Absentee ballot applications must reach county boards by 8:30 p.m. on Oct. 27; early in-person voting runs extended hours Oct. 26-30, and mail ballots must arrive by 7:30 p.m. on Nov. 3.
upcoming.why: Ohio's Senate race between Jon Husted and Sherrod Brown and its open governor race are both Cook Toss Ups.
upcoming.src: Ohio Secretary of State, accessed Oct 14

upcoming.title: Sand, Lahn debate on KCRG in Cedar Rapids
upcoming.what: Democrat Rob Sand and Republican Zach Lahn meet in a KCRG-TV debate in Cedar Rapids, now the first scheduled debate in the race after the Oct. 21 Iowa PBS debate was postponed.
upcoming.why: Iowa's open governorship is one of the competitive governor races, with Sand leading in the Marist and co/efficient polls.

upcoming.title: Talarico counter-rally at Texas Tech as Trump visits Lubbock
upcoming.what: Democrat James Talarico holds an evening rally at Texas Tech in Lubbock on Oct. 27, the day Trump campaigns for Ken Paxton at the Lubbock Memorial Civic Center (program 1 p.m., Trump 2:30 p.m. Central).
upcoming.why: Texas is a Cook Toss Up where Republican super PACs have spent at presidential scale; dueling events in a Republican stronghold test each side's closing turnout push.

upcoming.title: Nunn, Trone Garriott debate in Iowa's 3rd District
upcoming.what: Rep. Zach Nunn and Democrat Sarah Trone Garriott debate on KCCI at 9 p.m. Central.
upcoming.why: It is the only scheduled debate in a Republican-held Des Moines seat the DCCC has targeted with coordinated ads.

upcoming.title: Obama rallies in Atlanta for Ossoff, Bottoms
upcoming.what: Former President Barack Obama headlines a rally in Atlanta for Sen. Jon Ossoff and governor nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms; the location is to be emailed to RSVPs 24 hours ahead.
upcoming.why: It comes in the last days of Georgia's early voting, with a Toss Up governor race on the ballot and Senate super PACs on both sides off Georgia broadcast TV.

upcoming.title: Maine no-excuse absentee voting period ends
upcoming.what: Oct. 29 is the last day of Maine's no-excuse absentee period, including in-person absentee voting at town and city halls.
upcoming.why: The deadline shapes early ballots in the Collins-Jackson Senate race and the ME-02 House race.

upcoming.title: Kentucky early in-person voting begins
upcoming.what: Kentucky's three days of no-excuse early in-person voting run Thursday, Oct. 29, through Saturday, Oct. 31.
upcoming.why: Early votes begin in the open KY-06, which Inside Elections moved to Tilt Republican on Oct. 20, and the Barr-Booker Senate race.

upcoming.title: Pingree, Russell debate in Maine's 1st District
upcoming.what: Maine Public hosts a debate between Rep. Chellie Pingree and Republican Ron Russell at 7 p.m. on its radio, television and streams.
upcoming.why: It is the only scheduled debate in a Democratic-held seat that becomes competitive only in a Republican year.

upcoming.title: Bresnahan debates Democratic challenger on WVIA in PA-08
upcoming.what: WVIA hosts a PA-08 debate in Pittston at 7 p.m. between Rep. Rob Bresnahan and his Democratic challenger.
upcoming.why: Cook rates PA-08 a Toss Up and Inside Elections moved it to Tilt Democratic on Oct. 20; it is one of the Republican-held seats Democrats need for a majority.

upcoming.title: Georgia and Texas in-person early voting ends
upcoming.what: Friday, Oct. 30, is the last day of in-person early voting in Georgia and in Texas.
upcoming.why: The final early-vote totals in two Senate battlegrounds and the Georgia and Texas governor races set the Election Day math for both parties.
upcoming.src: Axios Atlanta, Oct 19; FOX 7 Austin, Oct 12

upcoming.title: Nevada polls close; Alaska follows after midnight ET
upcoming.what: Polls close at 10 p.m. ET in Nevada and Montana; most of Alaska closes at midnight ET and the Aleutian Islands at 1 a.m. ET on Nov. 4.
upcoming.why: Alaska's Senate race, rated a Toss-up by Inside Elections, is likely to be among the last competitive contests to report.

upcoming.title: First polls close in Indiana and Kentucky
upcoming.what: Polls in the Eastern time portions of Indiana and Kentucky close at 6 p.m. ET, with the rest of both states closing at 7 p.m. ET.
upcoming.why: The first returns of the night include House races such as KY-06, which Inside Elections moved to Lean Republican.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia, most of Florida
upcoming.what: Polls close at 7 p.m. ET in Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia and Vermont, in most of Florida (the western Panhandle at 8 p.m. ET) and at most New Hampshire polling places (all by 8 p.m. ET).
upcoming.why: First returns arrive in the Georgia, South Carolina, Florida and New Hampshire Senate races and the Georgia and Florida governor races.

upcoming.title: Polls close in North Carolina and Ohio
upcoming.what: Polls close at 7:30 p.m. ET in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia.
upcoming.why: Results begin in the North Carolina and Ohio Senate races and the Ohio governor race.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Maine, Pennsylvania, most of Michigan, Texas
upcoming.what: Polls close at 8 p.m. ET in Maine, Pennsylvania and the rest of New Hampshire, and in most of Michigan, Texas and Kansas, whose westernmost areas close at 9 p.m. ET.
upcoming.why: First results arrive in the Maine, Michigan, Texas and Kansas Senate races and the Michigan and Texas governor races.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Arizona
upcoming.what: Polls close at 9 p.m. ET in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin and Arizona.
upcoming.why: Results begin in the Iowa, Minnesota and Nebraska Senate races and the Iowa, Wisconsin and Arizona governor races.
